newsitem.title: USA: Guzman & Co. settles Dade County, Fla., lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Guzman & Co. settles Dade County, Fla., lawsuit.

text.p: Florida's Dade County and bond firm Guzman & Co have settled a lawsuit filed by the firm after the county removed it from the underwriting syndicate for a water-sewer bond issue, company president Leo Guzman said Wednesday.
The out-of-court agreement was signed late Tuesday and gives Guzman an extra $26 million of bonds to sell in upcoming Dade deals.
Guzman & Co is part of a standing pool of underwriters for Dade bond issues.

The county removed Guzman from the $450 million water-sewer deal in December amid controversy over a letter that accused one of the county's financial advisers, Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc, of violating securites regulations governing certain fees.
The letter was written on what appeared to be Guzman & Co letterhead and purportedly signed by Guzman, who insisted it was a forgery and asked federal regulators to investigate.
Guzman sued the county, claiming the removal was improper.

He said the settlement would give his firm about $175,000 in commissions, less than the $5 million it would have made on the original deal and not nearly enough to compensate for damage to the firm's reputation.
"You've got to realize your reputation is dragged through the dirt," Guzman said. However, he said, "This is probably all the county can do."
He said he agreed to settle because "It's not a good business practice to have an ongoing litigation with a major client."
The firm also sued another Miami bond firm, Howard Gary & Co., after reviewing phone records that Guzman said showed the phony fax was sent from the home of a Gary partner's relative.
That lawsuit is still pending and seeks treble damages totalling $15 million. Through its lawyer, the Gary firm denied sending the letter and condemned the incident.
Dade County officials were not immediately available for comment but provided a copy of the settlement agreement.
